text:
Large MoE models, powered by your SSD 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 Website  · 
 Blog  · 
 Slack  · 
 Apache-2.0 
 
 macOS / Metal  ·  Linux / CUDA  ·  Windows (in progress) 

 Run models larger than your RAM or VRAM. InferSSD builds on llama.cpp to run large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models from SSD, using standard GGUF files, with browser chat and an OpenAI-compatible API. It supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 , Muse-Spark-Open , Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8 Flash Next , plus ordinary RAM inference for Gemma4 E4B .

 Models

These are the tested GGUF files, community conversions of the named model releases. DeepSeek's Q8 0 keeps the official bit widths: routed experts stay native 4-bit MXFP4, and FP8 tensors become 8-bit Q8 0. See weight-format details.

 Model Parameter count GGUF reference 
 --- --- --- 
 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 763B total / 8–16B active mrfakename · Q8 0 
 Muse-Spark-Open 816B total / 42B active Unsloth · UD-Q4 K XL 
 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 35B total / 3B active Unsloth · UD-Q4 K XL 
 Qwen3.8 Flash Next 177B total / A3B Bartowski · IQ4 XS 
 Gemma4 E4B 7.46B total / E4B Google · QAT Q4 0 

Gemma uses the ordinary native loader without SSD expert offload. Before loading, the shared
launcher checks that weights, KV cache and working memory fit the memory budget, the machine's
physical memory unless a smaller one is configured; the system pages other memory out to make
room. On Apple silicon the per-layer embedding table, 2.15 GiB of the 4.80 GiB file, stays in the
file and its rows are read from the SSD as tokens use them; the other weights are held in memory.
A model that does not fit is rejected. macOS and Windows use the same model selection and launch
entry points.

 Performance benchmarks

 4K prompt tier · 256 output tokens · decode measured over tokens 129–256. All rates are in token/s ; higher is faster. The multiple next to each InferSSD rate is its speedup over llama.cpp on the same hardware. On the MacBook Pro, Colibri runs the official Safetensors on CPU; llama.cpp and InferSSD run the GGUF with Metal. See measurement details.

 Test hardware

 Hardware CPU (cores) GPU Memory SSD 
 --- --- --- --- --- 
 MacBook Pro Apple M5 Max (18) 40-core 48 GB unified 2 TB internal 
 RTX 5060 Ti Intel Core 3 100U (6) RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB + 16 GB VRAM 2 TB PCIe 4 ×4 
 RTX 5090 Intel Core Ultra 5 230F (10) RTX 5090 32 GB + 32 GB VRAM 2 TB PCIe 5 ×4 
 DGX Spark NVIDIA GB10 (20) Blackwell 128 GB unified 4 TB PCIe 5 ×4 

Unified memory is shared by the CPU and GPU. SSD capacities are nominal. See hardware details for SSD models, CPU core layouts, and configuration notes.

 Get started

Install on Apple Silicon macOS, or on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU or an AMD GPU with ROCm:

 

Each numbered release includes checked prebuilt packages for Apple Silicon macOS 15 or later and Windows 10 or 11 x64, built from the same tagged commit. Its installers download that exact release without developer tools; see the macOS package and Windows package. Linux builds that release from source for the machine's CPU and GPU, which takes about 2 to 12 minutes. The installer on main downloads the latest published package:

 

The installer works in a private environment and uses no sudo . A source build needs Git, Python 3.9 or later, and a C/C++ compiler. On macOS it also needs the Xcode Command Line Tools; Linux also needs systemd with cgroup v2, and the CUDA toolkit on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU or the ROCm HIP SDK on a machine whose AMD GPU runs on ROCm. Follow the printed PATH instruction if it shows one.

Then start a model:

 

For Muse, use unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF ; for Qwen3.6, unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF ; for Flash Next, bartowski/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF ; for Gemma, google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4 0-gguf . With serve , open in your browser, or point any OpenAI-compatible client at Add --host 0.0.0.0 to reach it from other devices on your network; the API has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the port can use it.

The first run downloads the model files (about 470 GiB for DeepSeek or Muse, 21 GiB for Qwen3.6) to /.local/share/inferssd/models and measures your machine. Use --model-dir /path/on/ssd to choose the drive, or -m /path/to/first-shard.gguf for files you already have. There is no memory setting to choose: InferSSD uses the memory available. Stop with Ctrl+C , or /exit in chat.

See the quick start for upgrades and uninstalling.

 Versions

InferSSD has a release number, 0.1.4 in framework/pyproject.toml , and every build has a
label of its own, . . : the day (UTC) of the commit it was built from, the
branch's commit count up to that commit, and the commit. The installer records the three in
 engine-resources.json beside the build, from the clone's Git me

install.title: Get started
install.html:
Install on Apple Silicon macOS, or on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU or an AMD GPU with ROCm:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/wici-ai/inferssd/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

Each numbered release includes checked prebuilt packages for Apple Silicon macOS 15 or later and Windows 10 or 11 x64, built from the same tagged commit. Its installers download that exact release without developer tools; see the macOS package and Windows package. Linux builds that release from source for the machine's CPU and GPU, which takes about 2 to 12 minutes. The installer on main downloads the latest published package:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wici-ai/inferssd/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

The installer works in a private environment and uses no sudo. A source build needs Git, Python 3.9 or later, and a C/C++ compiler. On macOS it also needs the Xcode Command Line Tools; Linux also needs systemd with cgroup v2, and the CUDA toolkit on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU or the ROCm HIP SDK on a machine whose AMD GPU runs on ROCm. Follow the printed PATH instruction if it shows one.

Then start a model:

# Chat in your terminal
inferssd cli -hf mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF

# Or start the web UI and an OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:8080
inferssd serve -hf mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF

For Muse, use unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF; for Qwen3.6, unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF; for Flash Next, bartowski/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF; for Gemma, google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf. With serve, open http://127.0.0.1:8080 in your browser, or point any OpenAI-compatible client at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. Add --host 0.0.0.0 to reach it from other devices on your network; the API has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the port can use it.

The first run downloads the model files (about 470 GiB for DeepSeek or Muse, 21 GiB for Qwen3.6) to ~/.local/share/inferssd/models and measures your machine. Use --model-dir /path/on/ssd to choose the drive, or -m /path/to/first-shard.gguf for files you already have. There is no memory setting to choose: InferSSD uses the memory available. Stop with Ctrl+C, or /exit in chat.

See the quick start for upgrades and uninstalling.
